title: Probability Foundations
relevance: Campus OAs and SDE interviews routinely test coin/dice/card counting, combinations, addition/complement, independence, and simple conditional probability as quick aptitude filters.
company_notes: Amazon appears in a QA/server-selection wrapped combinatorial OA variant.

phases.goal: Establish the core probability formulas and how to read a finite sample space.

must_hit.point: P(E) equals favourable outcomes over total outcomes, and every probability satisfies 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the classical ratio definition and the 0-to-1 bound without inventing extra axioms.

must_hit.point: The complement rule is P(E') = 1 − P(E); independence gives P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B); conditional is P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B); addition is P(A ∪ B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A ∩ B).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites complement, independence, conditional, and addition formulas as distinct tools.

must_hit.point: For two fair coins, sample space {HH, HT, TH, TT} has 4 outcomes and at least one head has probability 3/4.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the four equally likely outcomes and counts the three with a head.

probes: What is P(E) for equally likely outcomes, and how do you get the probability that an event does not happen?

hints.1: Start from favourable over total, then think about the opposite event.
hints.2: Write P(E') = 1 − P(E), and name addition, independence, and conditional if asked.
hints.3: For two coins, total 4; at least one head is HH, HT, TH so 3/4.

phases.goal: Show correct counting on dice, cards, combinations, and successive draws.

must_hit.point: Two fair dice have 36 outcomes; exactly five pairs sum to 8, so P(sum=8)=5/36; for sum S≥8 the ways shortcut is 13−S.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses 6×6=36, lists five sum-8 pairs or applies 13−8=5, and states 5/36.

must_hit.point: From a 52-card deck, red face cards are 3 face ranks times 2 red suits = 6 cards, so P(red face card)=6/52=3/26.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines face cards as Jacks, Queens, Kings; multiplies by two red suits; simplifies 6/52 to 3/26.

must_hit.point: Without replacement, P(all 3 green from 4 red and 5 green) is ⁵C₃/⁹C₃ = 5/42, equivalently (5/9)×(4/8)×(3/7).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Either uses combinations over ⁹C₃ or multiplies shrinking green counts and gets 5/42.

must_hit.point: Product of two dice is even via complement: both odd has probability (1/2)×(1/2)=1/4, so P(even product)=3/4.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Identifies odd×odd as the only odd product case and subtracts from 1.

probes: Two dice are rolled; what is P(sum is 8), and how does the dice-sum shortcut check your count?

hints.1: Fix the total sample size before listing favourable outcomes.
hints.2: For two dice use 36; for sum 8 either list pairs or use ways = 13−S when S≥8.

phases.goal: Choose between complement vs enumeration and with vs without replacement.

must_hit.point: For independent 'at least one' success, prefer 1−P(all fail); three archers with hit probs 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 give miss product (1/2)×(2/3)×(3/4)=1/4, so at least one hit is 3/4.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Immediately switches to none-hit product and subtracts from 1 to get 3/4.

must_hit.point: 'Drawn at random' defaults to without replacement (combinations or shrinking fractions); only explicit with-replacement yields independent repeats like (5/9)³.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the default without-replacement reading and contrasts the with-replacement independent product.

must_hit.point: Addition needs the intersection term: P(M∪P)=0.6+0.5−0.3=0.8, otherwise double-counting both.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Applies P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B) and warns that omitting the intersection overshoots.

probes: When should you use 1−P(all fail) instead of enumerating every 'at least one' case?

hints.1: Look for 'at least one' across independent trials.
hints.2: Compute each miss probability, multiply, subtract from 1.
hints.3: Archers: misses 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 → none hit 1/4 → at least one 3/4.

phases.goal: Apply conditional probability and OA-wrapped combinatorial patterns including derangements.

must_hit.point: Given sum of two dice is 8, the reduced space has 5 outcomes and only (3,5) has first die 3, so the conditional probability is 1/5.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Restricts to the five sum-8 pairs and counts one favourable → 1/5.

must_hit.point: Given at least one of two children is a boy, the reduced space is {BB, BG, GB}, so P(both boys)=1/3, not 1/2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Drops GG, keeps three equally likely outcomes, and picks only BB.

must_hit.point: Hypergeometric OA wrap: 20 servers with 4 faulty and 16 good, choose 3 with exactly one faulty is (⁴C₁×¹⁶C₂)/²⁰C₃ = 8/19.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Frames as choose 1 from faulty and 2 from good over choose 3 from 20, arriving at 8/19.

must_hit.point: Derangement of 4 letters: !4=9 and 4!=24, so P(no letter in correct envelope)=9/24=3/8.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses !4=9 over 24 permutations and simplifies to 3/8.

probes: Given the sum of two dice is 8, what is P(first die shows 3)?

hints.1: Condition by shrinking the sample space to outcomes that satisfy the given.
hints.2: List the five sum-8 pairs and see how many have first die 3.
hints.3: Only (3,5) works among five, so answer is 1/5.

tradeoffs.topic: Complement (1 − P(all fail)) vs enumerating every 'at least one' case
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For independent trials asking for at least one success, compute the all-fail product and subtract from 1; this avoids summing overlapping hit patterns, as with the three archers yielding 3/4.

'Drawn at random' means without replacement unless stated otherwise—use combinations or shrinking successive fractions. Explicit with replacement keeps the same fraction each draw (independent product).

tradeoffs.topic: Addition rule with intersection vs naively adding probabilities
tradeoffs.strong_answer: P(A ∪ B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A ∩ B); dropping the intersection double-counts overlap, e.g. 0.6+0.5−0.3=0.8 for passing at least one subject.

gotchas.trap: Treating 1 as a prime when a die shows a prime.
gotchas.correction: On {1,2,3,4,5,6} the primes are only {2,3,5}, so P(prime)=3/6=1/2.

gotchas.trap: Assuming 'drawn at random' means with replacement / independent repeats.
gotchas.correction: Default is without replacement; with-replacement independence applies only when the problem says so.

gotchas.trap: Given at least one boy in a two-child family, answering 1/2 that both are boys.
gotchas.correction: Conditioning removes only GG, leaving {BB, BG, GB}, so P(both boys | at least one boy)=1/3.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting the intersection when summing 'multiple of 3 or multiple of 4' dice sums.
